requirement_text.REQ-063: Execute Decision 0006's D1 (docs/migration/decisions/0006-identity-tables-schema-per-tenant.md): relocate REQ-015's users, groups and tenant_role tables out of the public default schema and into each tenant's own Postgres schema, via the same :prefix mechanism and the same TenantProvisioning.tenant_scoped_migrations/0 registry every business table already uses. See handoffs/WF02-REQ063-20260818/step-01-code-designer.json for the full original requirement text. Design (approved, PASS on re-gate after 1 rework): lib/letflow/design/req063-identity-tables-schema-per-tenant.md, including its §5b addition (provision_oidc_user's prefix-threading fix, added during rework).

task.description:
Implement lib/letflow/design/req063-identity-tables-schema-per-tenant.md in full -- every section (§2 the three tenant-scoped migrations, §3 the tenant_scoped_migrations/0 manifest entries, §4 the data-copy Mix task, §5 the separate guarded drop migration, §5b the identity.ex/auth_pipeline.ex prefix-threading changes). Read the design doc in full before writing any code -- it is the approved, gated spec; do not deviate from its function signatures or migration shapes without flagging why.

Ordering matters and is not optional (design §4, decision 0006 §4): the three create migrations must exist and be registered in tenant_scoped_migrations/0 before the data-copy task can run; the drop migration must be a separate file from the create migrations, per GBL-112's precedent, and must not run automatically as part of this same PR's migration set -- confirm with the design doc's own stated guard mechanism (§5) whether it's safe to include in this PR or whether it should be present-but-inert until a deliberate follow-up trigger. If the design leaves the guard mechanism itself as an open question (§7 item 3 originally did), make a reasoned engineering call, state it explicitly in your handoff's result.summary, and flag it for REVIEWER -- do not silently invent a guard with no explanation.

Self-review checklist (WF-02 §2a, plus this run's own specifics):
- mix compile --warnings-as-errors must exit 0 (the compile gate is currently clean on main post-ISS-0046 -- do not reintroduce warnings)
- mix ecto.migrate applies cleanly against a real/Docker Postgres for all three new create migrations AND the drop migration, run against a test tenant schema
- No string interpolation of tenant/user input into raw SQL (INV-7) -- if the data-copy task or drop migration needs any raw SQL fragment, confirm it matches TenantProvisioning's existing identifier-safety pattern (schema_name only ever comes from schema_name_for_tenant/1's own validated output, never from external input)
- provision_oidc_user's new prefix option is never caller-supplied from outside AuthPipeline's own resolved tenant_id -- matches this project's existing tenant_id-derivation discipline (see task.ex/token.ex's moduledoc precedent, though note those specific moduledoc blocks belong to REQ-064's future scope, not this one)
- Every existing caller of provision_oidc_user/3 (grep for it) still compiles after the arity change to /4 -- lib/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline.ex is the only known caller per the design, confirm no other caller exists
- New public functions have a one-line @doc

This requirement does NOT drop tenant_id from users/groups (design §1 scope boundary, reserved for REQ-064) -- do not remove the field from Identity.User/Identity.Group's schema modules.
acceptance_criteria: All migrations (3 create + 1 drop) apply cleanly against a fresh DB via mix ecto.migrate
users, groups and tenant_role each provision correctly inside a tenant schema when replay_migrations/2 runs against it
No SQL string interpolation of tenant/user data
provision_oidc_user/4's new prefix option and every caller in its private chain compiles and matches the approved design's signatures
lib/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline.ex's call site correctly derives and passes the prefix
All callers of the changed provision_oidc_user signature still compile
